name: Sewers
summary: In the hills west of Lordaeron's ruined palace, the Sewers open a second way into the Undercity. Bat handlers and travelers pass through the old stone channels to reach its inner rings.

sections.title: A Backdoor into the Catacombs
sections.body:
The Sewers once carried water away from Lordaeron's royal capital. Now Sylvanas Windrunner's Forsaken have folded those old channels into the Undercity's defenses. The passage opens west of the surface ruins near a Scarlet Watchtower in Tirisfal Glades, then slopes into the city.

Forsaken bat handlers carry riders through the cavernous passage to the Undercity's underground rings, clear of the slow cage lifts. Yet the route also skirts the fortified courtyards. Hostile infiltrators seek to exploit that weakness.

faq.q: Where does the sewer tunnel lead outside?
faq.answer: The sewer passage opens in the hills of Tirisfal Glades, west of the main gates to the Ruins of Lordaeron. The Scarlet Watchtower overlooking the lake is nearby.

faq.q: Why would anyone use the sewers instead of the main entrance?
faq.answer: The main entrance descends from the palace ruins by iron cage elevators, which can be slow and dangerous during an attack. The Sewers offer Forsaken bat traffic a direct, sloped route and a quick way out without waiting for the lifts.

faq.q: Is the sewer safe from Alliance raiders?
faq.answer: No. The Sewers bypass Lordaeron's fortified gatehouse and throne room, leaving a breach point for Alliance scouts and strike teams seeking to enter the Forsaken capital unseen.

angles.text: For the Forsaken, the Sewers keep the Undercity connected to the rest of Lordaeron. They carry bat traffic and ease the crowds at the courtyard elevators.
If you assault the Forsaken capital, the Sewers offer a hidden route past the heavily defended surface ruins.
